categories.nt-lxx: New Testament follows the Septuagint where it differs from the Hebrew
categories.nt-mt: New Testament follows the Hebrew where it differs from the Septuagint
categories.nt-neither: New Testament wording matches neither the Hebrew nor the Septuagint
categories.narrative: New Testament detail differs from the Old Testament account
categories.book: Whole-book differences between the Hebrew and the Septuagint

abbrev.MT: Masoretic Text (the standard Hebrew text, Leningrad Codex c. 1008 AD)

items.title: Young woman / virgin
items.mt: ʿalmah — "young woman" (of marriageable age)
items.lxx: parthenos — usually "virgin"
items.ntr: parthenos — "virgin" (as the LXX)
items.note: The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ) reads ʿalmah like the MT. How narrowly ʿalmah and parthenos should be translated is itself debated.
scholars: Rashi (11th century) — the young woman is the prophet's wife
Justin Martyr, Dialogue with Trypho (2nd century) — the earliest recorded debate over the word

items.title: Ears / a body
items.mt: "ears you have dug (opened) for me"
items.lxx: "a body you have prepared for me" (most manuscripts; a few read "ears")
items.ntr: "a body you have prepared for me"
items.note: Hebrew verse 7 = English 6. Hebrews builds its argument (10:10) on the word "body".

items.title: "Let all God's angels worship him"
items.mt: Shorter verse; no line about angels or gods worshipping
items.lxx: Longer verse, including "let all the sons/angels of God worship him" and "rejoice, O nations, with his people"
items.ntr: Heb 1:6 "let all God's angels worship him"; Rom 15:10 "rejoice, O Gentiles, with his people"
items.note: A Dead Sea Scroll (4QDeutq) has a longer Hebrew text close to the LXX ("bow down to him, all gods"), so the shorter MT may be the changed text here.

items.title: My son / his children
items.mt: "out of Egypt I called my son"
items.lxx: "out of Egypt I called his children"
items.ntr: "out of Egypt I called my son" (as the Hebrew)
items.note: Matthew's point (Jesus as God's son) depends on the Hebrew wording.

items.title: Edom / mankind
items.mt: "that they may possess the remnant of Edom"
items.lxx: "that the rest of mankind may seek [the Lord]"
items.ntr: "that the rest of mankind may seek the Lord" (as the LXX)
items.note: In Hebrew consonants, Edom (ʾdwm) / mankind (ʾdm) and possess (yyršw) / seek (ydršw) differ by one letter each. James's argument for including Gentiles uses the LXX reading.

items.title: Where is the voice?
items.mt: "A voice cries: In the wilderness prepare the way… make straight in the desert a highway for our God"
items.lxx: "A voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way… make straight the paths of our God"
items.ntr: "A voice of one crying in the wilderness" (as the LXX); "his paths"
items.note: The Hebrew consonants allow either phrasing; the MT's division comes from medieval accent marks. The Qumran community (1QS 8:14) read it the MT way.

items.title: "Make their heart fat" / "their heart has grown dull"
items.mt: Commands to the prophet: "Make the heart of this people fat… shut their eyes"
items.lxx: Description: "the heart of this people has grown dull… they have closed their eyes"
items.ntr: Matthew and Acts: "has grown dull… they have closed" (as the LXX)
items.note: In the LXX form the people harden themselves; in the Hebrew the prophet is told to harden them. See also John 12:40 (separate entry).

items.title: "He has blinded their eyes"
items.mt: The prophet is told to blind and harden
items.lxx: The people have closed their own eyes
items.ntr: "He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart" — God as the one acting
items.note: John's wording is a free rendering closer to the sense of the Hebrew than to the LXX.

items.title: "In vain do they worship me"
items.mt: "their fear of me is a commandment of men learned by rote"
items.lxx: "in vain do they worship me, teaching the commandments and doctrines of men"
items.ntr: "in vain do they worship me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men" (as the LXX)

items.title: Strength / praise
items.mt: "out of the mouth of babes… you have established strength"
items.lxx: "out of the mouth of babes… you have prepared praise"
items.ntr: "you have prepared praise" (as the LXX)
items.note: Jesus's reply to the priests uses "praise," fitting the children's shouts in the temple.

items.title: Sight to the blind
items.mt: "opening to those who are bound" (peqaḥ-qoaḥ, "opening," often of eyes)
items.lxx: "recovery of sight to the blind"
items.ntr: "recovery of sight to the blind" (as the LXX), plus "to set at liberty the oppressed" from Isa 58:6 LXX
items.note: Luke presents this as the scroll Jesus read in the Nazareth synagogue.

items.title: Pierced / mocked
items.mt: "they will look on me whom they have pierced"
items.lxx: "they will look to me because they have mocked [me]" (lit. "danced in triumph")
items.ntr: "they will look on him whom they pierced" (Hebrew sense, third person)
items.note: John's Greek is close to the later Greek revision of Theodotion rather than the LXX.

items.title: Bed / staff
items.mt: "Israel bowed himself upon the head of the bed" (miṭṭah)
items.lxx: "Israel bowed in worship on the top of his staff" (maṭṭeh)
items.ntr: "worshipped, leaning on the top of his staff" (as the LXX)
items.note: Same Hebrew consonants (mṭh); the words differ only in vowels, which were added to the text much later.

items.title: Seventy / seventy-five souls
items.mt: 70 persons went down to Egypt (Gen 46:27; Exod 1:5; Deut 10:22)
items.lxx: 75 persons (Gen 46:27; Exod 1:5)
items.ntr: Stephen: "seventy-five souls"
items.note: Two Dead Sea Scrolls (4QExodᵇ, 4QGen-Exodᵃ) also read 75 at Exod 1:5.

items.title: The second Cainan
items.mt: Arphaxad is the father of Shelah (no Cainan)
items.lxx: Arphaxad → Cainan → Shelah (Gen 10:24; 11:12–13)
items.ntr: "…the son of Shelah, the son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad" (as the LXX)
items.note: 1 Chronicles 1:18, 24 in the MT also lack this Cainan.

items.title: "I was a husband to them" / "I disregarded them"
items.mt: "my covenant which they broke, although I was a husband to them"
items.lxx: "they did not continue in my covenant, and I disregarded them"
items.ntr: "and I disregarded them" (as the LXX)
items.note: The Hebrew verbs for "be husband/master" (bʿlty) and "loathe/reject" (gʿlty) differ by one letter.

items.title: Meribah and Massah / the rebellion and the testing
items.mt: Place names: "as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah"; "forty years I loathed that generation"
items.lxx: "as in the provocation, as in the day of testing"
items.ntr: "as in the rebellion, in the day of testing"; links "forty years" to "saw my works"

items.title: "God opposes the proud"
items.mt: "Surely he scorns the scorners, but gives grace to the humble"
items.lxx: "The Lord resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble"
items.ntr: "God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble" (as the LXX)

items.title: "Will not be put to shame"
items.mt: "whoever believes will not be in haste (panic)"
items.lxx: "whoever believes in him will not be put to shame"
items.ntr: "will not be put to shame" (as the LXX)

items.title: 430 years — in Egypt only?
items.mt: Israel lived in Egypt 430 years
items.lxx: 430 years "in the land of Egypt and in the land of Canaan" (SP similar)
items.ntr: Paul counts 430 years from the promise to Abraham to the Law
items.note: Paul's count fits the LXX/SP reading, which includes the patriarchs' time in Canaan.

items.title: Did Abram leave Haran after Terah died?
items.mt: Terah is 70 at Abram's birth (11:26), Abram leaves at 75 (12:4), Terah dies at 205 — i.e. 60 years later
items.lxx: Same numbers as the MT
items.ntr: Stephen: Abram moved "after his father died"
items.note: The Samaritan Pentateuch gives Terah's age at death as 145, which agrees with Acts. Others suggest Abram was not Terah's firstborn.

items.title: Which tomb, which seller?
items.mt: Abraham buys Machpelah at Hebron from Ephron the Hittite (Gen 23); Jacob buys land at Shechem from the sons of Hamor (Gen 33:19; Josh 24:32)
items.lxx: Same as the MT
items.ntr: Stephen: the tomb at Shechem "that Abraham bought… from the sons of Hamor"
items.note: Often explained as Stephen compressing two purchases into one summary.

items.title: Abiathar or Ahimelech?
items.mt: David receives the bread from Ahimelech the priest (1 Sam 21:1–6)
items.lxx: Abimelech (spelling variant) — still not Abiathar
items.ntr: "in the time of Abiathar the high priest"
items.note: Matthew 12:4 and Luke 6:4 omit the name, and some manuscripts of Mark omit the phrase. Abiathar was Ahimelech's son and later high priest.

items.title: Jeremiah or Zechariah?
items.mt: Thirty pieces of silver thrown "to the potter" in the house of the LORD — in Zechariah
items.lxx: "into the furnace" (to test the metal)
items.ntr: Matthew attributes the quotation to "Jeremiah the prophet"
items.note: Commonly explained as a combined quotation drawing on Jeremiah's potter and field purchase (Jer 18–19; 32:6–15), named after the more prominent prophet.

items.title: To Zion / from Zion
items.mt: "A redeemer will come to Zion"
items.lxx: "The deliverer will come for Zion's sake"
items.ntr: "The deliverer will come from Zion"
items.note: Paul's "from" matches neither text; he may be blending Ps 14:7 ("salvation out of Zion").

items.title: Received gifts / gave gifts
items.mt: "you received gifts among men"
items.lxx: "you received gifts for man"
items.ntr: "he gave gifts to men"
items.note: The Aramaic Targum and the Syriac Peshitta of the Psalm also read "gave," so Paul may follow a known interpretive tradition.

items.title: Little / by no means least
items.mt: "Bethlehem Ephrathah, too little to be among the clans of Judah"
items.lxx: "Bethlehem, house of Ephrathah, very few to be among the thousands of Judah"
items.ntr: "Bethlehem… are by no means least among the rulers of Judah"
items.note: Matthew's wording reverses the sense, presenting the town as honored because of the coming ruler.

items.title: "Death is swallowed up in victory"
items.mt: "he will swallow up death forever" (lāneṣaḥ — "forever," in Aramaic also "victory")
items.lxx: "death, having prevailed, swallowed [them] up"
items.ntr: "Death is swallowed up in victory"
items.note: Paul's wording agrees with the later Greek version of Theodotion and is closer to the Hebrew.

items.title: Galilee of the nations
items.mt: "the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations"
items.lxx: Differs in wording and adds "you who dwell…"
items.ntr: Follows the Hebrew more closely than the LXX
items.note: Hebrew 8:23–9:1 = English 9:1–2.

items.title: "Like a lion" / "they pierced"
items.mt: Most manuscripts: "like a lion [at] my hands and my feet" (kāʾărî)
items.lxx: "they dug (pierced) my hands and my feet"
items.note: A psalms scroll from Naḥal Ḥever (5/6ḤevPs) appears to read a verb (kʾrw), supporting a reading like the LXX. The NT does not quote this line directly.
scholars: Peter W. Flint, The Dead Sea Psalms Scrolls and the Book of Psalms (1997) — on the Naḥal Ḥever reading

items.title: Sons of Israel / sons of God
items.mt: "according to the number of the sons of Israel"
items.lxx: "according to the number of the angels (some manuscripts: sons) of God"
items.note: A Dead Sea Scroll (4QDeutʲ) reads "sons of God," supporting the LXX.
scholars: Emanuel Tov, Textual Criticism of the Hebrew Bible — treats 'sons of Israel' as a later theological change
Michael S. Heiser — reads 'sons of God' as the divine council (Ps 82)

items.title: "He will see light"
items.mt: "Out of the anguish of his soul he shall see [and] be satisfied"
items.lxx: "to show him light"
items.note: Three Isaiah scrolls from Qumran (1QIsaᵃ, 1QIsaᵇ, 4QIsaᵈ) also read "light."
scholars: Emanuel Tov and other text critics regard 'light' as the original reading; many modern translations (NIV, NRSV) include it

items.title: What Cain said
items.mt: "Cain spoke to Abel his brother. And when they were in the field…" (his words are missing)
items.lxx: Adds: "Let us go out into the field" (also SP, Syriac, Vulgate)

items.title: How tall was Goliath?
items.mt: six cubits and a span (about 9′9″)
items.lxx: four cubits and a span (about 6′9″)
items.note: The Samuel scroll from Qumran (4QSamᵃ) agrees with the LXX's four cubits.

items.title: Genealogy ages in Genesis 5 and 11
items.mt: Creation to the Flood: 1,656 years
items.lxx: Creation to the Flood: 2,242 years — many fathers are 100 years older when their son is born
items.note: The SP has a third set of numbers. These totals underlie different ancient dates for the age of the world.

items.title: Jeremiah: a shorter, rearranged book
items.mt: Longer text; oracles against the nations in chapters 46–51
items.lxx: About one-eighth shorter; the oracles against the nations follow 25:13 and are in a different order (so LXX chapter numbers differ from 25 on)
items.note: Hebrew fragments from Qumran (4QJerᵇ, 4QJerᵈ) support the shorter form — evidence that two Hebrew editions circulated.
scholars: Emanuel Tov — the Septuagint of Jeremiah reflects an earlier Hebrew edition, supported by 4QJerᵇ,ᵈ

items.title: David and Goliath: a shorter version
items.lxx: Codex Vaticanus lacks those passages, giving a shorter story in which David is not re-introduced to Saul

items.title: Job: about one-sixth shorter
items.mt: Ends at 42:17
items.lxx: Roughly a sixth shorter overall, and adds an ending after 42:17 identifying Job with Jobab, king of Edom

items.title: Esther and Daniel: added sections
items.mt: Esther never names God; Daniel has 12 chapters
items.lxx: Six additions to Esther (with prayers naming God); Daniel adds the Prayer of Azariah and Song of the Three, Susanna, and Bel and the Dragon

items.title: Psalm numbers are offset
items.mt: Psalms 9 and 10 are separate; 114 and 115 separate; 116 one psalm; 147 one psalm
items.lxx: Psalms 9–10 are one psalm, 114–115 one, 116 is split in two, 147 is split in two — so most LXX numbers are one lower (LXX 22 = Hebrew 23). LXX also adds Psalm 151
items.note: This app's Septuagint column converts the numbers for you.
